_readme: Accepted HIGH/CRITICAL advisories for `npm run check:dependency-audit:mobile` (run from the repo root).
Same contract as the web /.audit-allowlist.json — see its _readme for the field shapes and the rules.
Separate from the web allowlist ON PURPOSE: the two trees share almost nothing, and an accept reasoned
about a server code path means nothing inside an Expo bundle. Never paste an id between the two files
without re-arguing the reason for THAT tree.
Note the mobile gate covers the WHOLE tree, not just runtime deps: `--omit=dev` is inert under
`--package-lock-only` (verified 2026-08-07 — identical reports with and without it). That is the honest
posture for this tree anyway, since mobile's only devDependency is @babel/core.
Empty is the healthy state — the two linkify-it advisories that were briefly accepted here are fixed
instead, by the `linkify-it: ^5.0.2` override in mobile/package.json. See CHANGELOG 479.
The image-size accepts below are NOT fixable as of 2026-08-17: the vulnerable range is <= 2.0.2 and
2.0.2 is the LATEST published version — no patched release exists to bump or override to (upstream's
last release is 2025-04-02; verified against the GitHub advisories and the npm registry). Re-check
`npm view image-size versions` at expiry; the moment a patched release lands, fix via override on
metro's `image-size` dep and delete both entries.
The brace-expansion accepts (DEPAUDIT.5, 2026-09-30) ARE fixable, unlike image-size. TWO vulnerable copies sit in
mobile/package-lock.json and both accepts cover both (the allowlist gates by advisory id, not by copy): 2.1.4 via
@bacons/apple-targets > glob@10 > minimatch@9 (declares ^2.0.2, admits 2.1.7), and the root 5.0.9 via expo's
build tooling (@expo/cli, @expo/metro-config, @expo/fingerprint, @expo/config, expo-updates) > glob@13 > minimatch@10
(admits 5.0.12). `cd mobile && npm update brace-expansion --package-lock-only` moves both (a 12-line lockfile diff,
verified 30 Sep). They are accepted instead because mobile/package-lock.json is an OTA publish path and neither copy
is imported by app code (nothing under mobile/app, components or lib imports glob, minimatch or brace-expansion).
Take the lockfile bump with the next native release and delete both entries then.
The braces and node-forge accepts (DEPAUDIT.6, 2026-10-03) are NOT fixable, like image-size: braces' range is <= 3.0.3
and node-forge's is <= 1.4.0, both the LATEST published versions (checked `npm view <pkg> versions` and the GitHub
advisories 3 Oct: no first_patched_version). Both were proven absent from the shipped app the strong way: a local
`expo export --platform ios --source-maps` (the same Metro bundle eas update ships) lists 2666 source modules and
NONE of them is braces, micromatch, fast-glob, chokidar, tailwindcss, node-forge or @expo/code-signing-certificates.
Re-check at expiry; the moment a patched release lands, `npm update <pkg> --package-lock-only` with the next native
release and delete the entry.

accepted.reason: Build-time only, first-party input only. image-size is reached solely via expo > @expo/metro > metro (Assets.js), which parses the dimensions of image assets checked into THIS repo during bundling/export — it is not in the shipped app bundle and never parses attacker-supplied images. The DoS (infinite loop on a crafted ICNS file) could only hang our own build, and only if a malicious ICNS were committed to the repo. No patched version exists (vulnerable range <= 2.0.2 = every published release).

Same code path and posture as GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr: metro's build-time asset dimension probe over repo-owned images; JXL/HEIF infinite-loop variant. Not runtime-reachable in the app; worst case is a hung CI build from a malicious committed image. No patched version exists (vulnerable range <= 2.0.2 = every published release).

Build-time only, first-party input only. Two vulnerable copies, both covered: (a) 2.1.4 via @bacons/apple-targets (the WIDGET.1 Expo config plugin) > glob@10 > minimatch@9, whose only globSync calls use patterns hard-coded in the plugin (`./targets/*/expo-target.config.@(json|js)`, `preview/*.xcassets`, `_shared/*`, `*.entitlements`; app.config.js passes no root/match options); (b) the root 5.0.9 via expo's build tooling (@expo/cli, @expo/metro-config, @expo/fingerprint, @expo/config, expo-updates) > glob@13 > minimatch@10, globbing repo paths with patterns the tooling and this repo write. Both run on the build machine (config evaluation, prebuild, bundling, fingerprinting); nothing under mobile/app, mobile/components or mobile/lib imports glob, minimatch or brace-expansion, so no attacker-supplied pattern ever reaches brace expansion; the worst case is a hung build from a pattern we wrote ourselves. Variant: recursion in parseCommaParts (fixed in 2.1.5 / 5.0.10).

Build-time only, first-party input only. Two vulnerable copies, both covered: (a) 2.1.4 via @bacons/apple-targets (the WIDGET.1 Expo config plugin) > glob@10 > minimatch@9, whose only globSync calls use patterns hard-coded in the plugin (`./targets/*/expo-target.config.@(json|js)`, `preview/*.xcassets`, `_shared/*`, `*.entitlements`; app.config.js passes no root/match options); (b) the root 5.0.9 via expo's build tooling (@expo/cli, @expo/metro-config, @expo/fingerprint, @expo/config, expo-updates) > glob@13 > minimatch@10, globbing repo paths with patterns the tooling and this repo write. Both run on the build machine (config evaluation, prebuild, bundling, fingerprinting); nothing under mobile/app, mobile/components or mobile/lib imports glob, minimatch or brace-expansion, so no attacker-supplied pattern ever reaches brace expansion; the worst case is a hung build from a pattern we wrote ourselves. Variant: recursion on nested brace groups (fixed in 2.1.6 / 5.0.11).

Build-time only, first-party input only. One copy, braces 3.0.3, reached via (a) tailwindcss@3 (NativeWind's compiler, run by `withNativeWind` in metro.config.js) > micromatch / fast-glob / chokidar, expanding the content globs in mobile/tailwind.config.js (`./app/**/*.{js,jsx,ts,tsx}`, `./components/**/*.{js,jsx,ts,tsx}`); and (b) metro-file-map and @expo/metro-file-map > micromatch, matching the dev-server watcher's ignore/glob patterns from metro.config.js and expo's defaults. Every pattern is written by this repo or the tooling; all of it runs on the build machine (bundling, export, `expo start`). A local `expo export --platform ios --source-maps` shows none of braces, micromatch, fast-glob, chokidar or tailwindcss in the shipped bundle (NativeWind's runtime is react-native-css-interop, which does not import them), so no attacker-supplied pattern can ever reach brace expansion; the worst case is a stack overflow in our own build from a pattern we wrote. No patched version exists (vulnerable range <= 3.0.3 = every published release).

Build-time/CLI only, never verifies an attacker's signature. One copy, node-forge 1.4.0, reached via (a) expo > @expo/cli (utils/codesigning.js: signs dev-server manifests with the developer's own key, `signBufferRSASHA256AndVerify` re-verifies the signature it JUST made, `validateSelfSignedCertificate` checks a cert we generated against our own key pair; run/ios/codeSigning/Security.js only PARSES certs from the local macOS keychain) and (b) expo-updates > @expo/code-signing-certificates, imported ONLY by expo-updates/cli (generate/configure code-signing commands), not by expo-updates/build. The flaw is a forgery-acceptance bug in RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 VERIFY; none of these paths verifies a signature produced by anyone else. On the phone, update code signing (not even configured in app.config.js) would be verified natively by expo-updates' Swift/Kotlin, not JS. A local `expo export --platform ios --source-maps` shows neither node-forge nor @expo/code-signing-certificates in the shipped bundle (expo-updates contributes only its build/ runtime modules). No patched version exists (vulnerable range <= 1.4.0 = every published release).
